How many 4-5 stars leave football undrafted, by class (busts), and the undrafted pro share.

areas.name: Birth dates, ages and held-back boys
areas.shows: Each person's date of birth and his true age on any day. It also shows whether he is a year old for his class (held back or started school late), a year young (skipped a grade), or reclassified in high school, and his school age against his real age.
checks: Births by month against the CDC 2015-2023 curve (late-summer peak, spring low).
Held back about 10% overall: summer births 15-19%, September births 4%. A year young about 1%, mostly fall births.
Reclassifying: about 0.4% of 16-year-olds rated over 52 graduate early, and about 0.5% repeat a year. Nobody repeats twice.
Relative age effect: are boys who are old for their class rated higher and given more stars at the same potential? Influences should be noteworthy, never driving.
Age at college entry, at the draft (early entrants 21, seniors 22-23) and at retirement, by position. Oldest player each season, kickers and punters included.
Every season row's age matches the birth date (the engine age is his age on 31 August as the season starts).

areas.name: Names, heritage and ethnicity
areas.shows: Each player's full name (first, surname, suffix, hyphen, initials, DeAndre-style spellings) and his heritage group: White, Black, Hispanic, Polynesian, East, Southeast or South Asian. Ethnicity changes no rating; it only shapes names and faces, and follows who really plays at each level.
checks: Ethnic mix by level and year: high school by state against child population times participation; FBS near 48.9% Black (NCAA 2023); NFL share.
Mix by position (QB, OL, CB, K/P) against real roster shares.
Polynesian players concentrated in HI, UT and CA; Asian split by state (Hmong in MN and WI, Filipino in HI and NV, Indian in NJ and TX).
Same full name shared within a pool: 4.4% of 22,843 college roster players in 2024; 7.84% of all nflverse players. The most common names, such as 'Jayden Williams' (7 in 2024).

Suffix rates: Jr. 4.5%, II 1.2%, III 0.8%, IV 0.1% (1.6 times that among Black players). Hyphenated 0.8% (2.5% Hispanic). Goes by initials 3%. Inner-capital or apostrophe spellings for Black and Polynesian players only.
First names follow the birth decade (no 'Jayden' born in 1972), and the surname fits the heritage.
Ethnicity has no link to ratings or potential at the same level: mean overall by group within a level and position should match.

Combine invites per year (CalendarLog combine_invites) against the real count of about 330.
Pro day times faster than combine times for the same men.
Combine moments: at most one news item a year, only for a forty 0.12 s or more past 4.25 + 0.0042 x (weight - 180).

areas.name: The 67 attributes
areas.shows: Each player's 67 visible ratings (1-99, stored as decimals) in 8 groups: physical, passing, running, receiving, line play, defense, kicking and snapping, mental. Each has its own growth profile (maturity at 14, growth rate and window, coachability, experience weight, decline age and rate, injury sensitivity, fatigue).
checks: Distribution of each attribute by level, position and age. Mental reads should rise with age; speed should peak early.
Elite tails: how many 95+ speed, 95+ arm or 95+ kick power exist per season at each level.
Correlations that must hold (speed against weight, strength against anchor) and ones that must not exist (ethnicity against anything).
Skills a position does not use (a receiver's tackling, a lineman's catching) stay low and fade 1.5 a year after a move.
Each attribute against its real proxy: physical ones through the combine, play ones through the engine's per-player outcomes (see the stat lines).
No attribute stuck at 1 or 99 in large numbers; ratings never above their ceilings.

areas.name: Hidden traits: consistency, temperament, recovery, injury proneness, longevity, wear, bloom
areas.shows: Hidden game-day and body traits: consistency, temperament and recovery (1-20, drift with age), injury proneness (1-20, +1 per major injury), longevity (years added to every decline age), wear (adds up from major injuries and speeds up physical decline), and bloom (years his growth windows shift: early or late bloomer).
checks: Each trait's spread: about normal(10, 3.5) at creation; bloom normal(0, 1.1) clamped -2.5 to 3; longevity normal(0, 1.3) clamped -3 to 3.5.
Drift: consistency +0-0.25 and temperament +0-0.3 a year under 26; recovery -0.1 to -0.4 a year from 30.
Proneness rises after majors; wear goes up 1.5 per major; pros with wear over 6 retire earlier.
Late bloomers (+2 bloom): later full height and later growth. Do they get missed by recruiters and found later? Count drafted late bloomers with 2-3 stars.
Longevity against career length and decline age (do 34-year-old starters have high longevity?).

parts.notes:
Read-only stock-take; nothing built or changed. Main sources read: docs/reference/how-it-works/recruiting.md (checked at e66acb3 on 2026-10-28), struct definitions in crates/afm-engine/src/world/{mod,program,high_school,hs_year,hs_playoffs,schedule,college,polls,voters,ncaa,eligibility,deals,geo,news,charts}.rs and world/scouting/services.rs, the export writer crates/afm-tools/src/raw.rs (write_raw; world_trial.rs only calls it), first records of programs, high_schools, portal, lineups and meta in /mnt/project-files/afm/trials-10/seed-2026/raw/, data/real-world/README.md, rates.json, trial3_baselines.json, tools/dashboard/build_data.py real_values, and the real targets printed by world_trial.rs, dynasty_check.rs and calendar_check.rs.

Cross-cutting findings for the reader app:
1. The world file keeps only the current and previous college season in full: games, polls, brackets, bowl teams, conference membership, conference records, expected wins (World.college and World.college_prev, plus World.prev_polls). Past polls, bowls, playoff brackets, conference standings and schedules are gone. The game log keeps box scores, tags and loudness only. Neither the world nor the export says which past games were bowls, playoff games or title games, or gives their dates, sites, lines, crowds or weather. This is the biggest gap for checking seasons at the micro level.
2. ProgramSeason has no division or conference. The dashboard already works around this through news text (build_data.py balance).
3. Many World fields are stored but not exported: class_scores, recruiting_log.five_stars and transfer_seasons, ProgramEra (ledger, NIL offers, NCAA cases), hs_pipeline and area_pipeline, season_records, AD, collective trend, the history and dark years, prestige recent and prestige_rel, a high school's coach, playoff wins, semifinal, county, area and resources, the A3 eligibility counters, portal_by_division and graduate_transfers, people's walk_on, visibility, born, offers, visits and commit history, and high-school-only coaches (raw.rs filters them out). A reader that opens the world file directly gets most of these. Some are pub(crate), so the reader needs accessors in afm-engine or must live in that crate.
4. Some things are stored only as note text: high school transfers, the commit date, the offer count, summer school, special admits. A recruit's choice reasons are computed only for your own desk.
5. The trial-10 sample export is out of date: its signing_classes show the old 4,000 three-star and 2,000 two-star quotas, while the code now uses 2,800 and 3,200. meta.json carries no git commit (the world file header does), so a reader cannot tell which rules made an export. signing_classes also gets one entry per rating stage, so take the last entry for each year.
6. Several real references are memory, not data, and need a source before anyone tunes against them: high school scoring about 26, the 151-game streak, the D3 and NAIA playoff fields, the early-signing share of 80-90%, the FBS single-season records, the strict-admission bars and the deals' payouts. Gaps listed in data/real-world/README.md: NIL dollars per school, JUCO and prep signee counts, D2 portal counts, a high school playoff source for some states.

parts.notes:
I read the pages and code, built nothing and changed nothing. Main sources: docs/reference/how-it-works/staff-and-coaches.md, play-calling.md and training.md, plus the struct definitions in crates/afm-engine/src/world/coach.rs, staff.rs, program.rs (AthleticDirector, ProgramSeason, Program staff fields), high_school.rs, league.rs, pro/mod.rs, pro/office.rs, nfl_year.rs, systems.rs, trends.rs, records.rs (UnitBuzz), folk/life.rs, folk/staffing.rs, people.rs, training/mod.rs and seat.rs. The export writers are in crates/afm-tools/src/raw.rs.

Quirks I found in the data, worth checking before the reader trusts it:
1. Back-to-back college jobs overlap by one year. A college hire's `since` comes from cycle_year(w), but `leave` sets `to` to w.year (world/staff.rs, `hire` and `leave`). In coaches.jsonl, coach 0 (Larry Heger) is at Bethel 1988-1990 and Albany State from 1989, and the same pattern repeats at every move. Year-by-year staff rebuilt from stints will double-count.
2. Only head coaches get wins and losses (`credit_head`, the HS, NFL and other-league crediting). Every assistant stint and every spin-up stint reads 0-0.
3. Several things the reader needs are missing from the export:
   - coaches.jsonl leaves out coaches who only ever coached high school.
   - high_schools.jsonl has no coach id per season.
   - programs.jsonl has no OC, DC, position coaches, AD, installed systems or contract.
   - news.jsonl drops each item's date.
   - The support arrays leave out engagement.
   - None of these are exported: Train, World.trends, World.nfl_seasons, novelty, system_norms, coach ties, learning ceiling, sportsmanship and decline fields.
   All of them are in the world file.
4. Much of this part is computed at the moment it's used and never stored:
   - guidelines, styles, caller skills, hiring scores and offers;
   - AD reads and NFL owner badness, hot seat;
   - AI training weeks, drawn staff and road marks.
   A Rust reader can call the engine functions named above to show them for today only. Showing them for a past season needs new stored logs; I listed these under needs_new.
5. Only today's value is kept for coach ability, reputation, contracts, installed systems, the AD and the GM. Career sparklines need yearly snapshots.

The real coaching-market bands in docs/world-model.md ('Check run') are marked there as Claude's reading, not checked. They need sources before anyone judges against them.

Other parts own some neighbouring data:
- scouts and personnel staff (clubs[].scouts, nfl_clubs.jsonl scouts): scouting part;
- the Coaches Poll panel (world/voters.rs): polls part;
- hot-seat storylines (World.storylines): stories part;
- the coaches' pay line and buyouts on the books (World.finance): finance part;
- practice injuries: injuries part.

parts.notes:
I only read files and ran small reads of the exports. I built and changed nothing. The files I relied on: /home/user/AFM/crates/afm-engine/src/world/game_log.rs, /home/user/AFM/crates/afm-engine/src/game/stats.rs, /home/user/AFM/crates/afm-engine/src/world/records.rs, /home/user/AFM/crates/afm-engine/src/world/charts.rs, /home/user/AFM/crates/afm-tools/src/raw.rs (the AFM_RAW writer; world_trial.rs calls it), /home/user/AFM/crates/afm-tools/src/bin/match_check.rs, /home/user/AFM/tools/dashboard/build_data.py, and /home/user/AFM/data/real-world/.

**Where the data lives.** The game log is trial tooling only. World.game_log is marked #[serde(skip)], so box scores, situation totals, team situations, player season lines, lineups and NFL box scores exist only in the raw export, never in the world file. Without the export, the world file still has:
- the stat book (stats.*)
- program season totals
- nfl_seasons and nfl_champions
- each pro season's full StatLine
- high school seasons and hs_lines
- two seasons of level tallies and state polls (charts)
- this season's and last season's college games, with weather, lines, attendance, tags and kind (college and college_prev)
- the current NFL season with slots and lines (nfl_season)
- your team's kept whole games (seat_games)
- every NFL and college team's last two tapes (gameday.tapes)

**Defects and gaps found:**
- TeamStats.red_zone_trips and red_zone_tds are never incremented anywhere: 0 in all 143,682 college games of trial 10. The dashboard's rz_td_pct reads them.
- The box score's 'top' adds up play durations (ball-in-play time, about 266 s a team), not clock possession time.
- NFL games add no situation rows (add_nfl skips game_log::situations), and neither do high school games. So the NFL, with the richest real tables, has only team box scores in the world data.
- GameSummary has no game kind, date, week, site, weather, line or quarter scores. Playoffs and bowls can't be split out, and NFL playoff games sit among the regular games (285 a year from 2021).
- raw.rs drops these fields:
  - games: xp, two_point, punt_yds, cross
  - programs: epa, epa_allowed, plays_allowed
  - pros: the full StatLine
- These are never exported: nfl_seasons, the stat book's honors (All-America, all-conference, awards), the Heisman vote, the norms, and the charts.
- The college book drops many StatLine fields (XP attempts, FG attempts by distance band, kickoffs, punts inside the 20, QB hits and hurries, wins by speed, power and finesse, penalties, top speed and more).
- High school games keep no per-game results log.
- hs_lines are exported only for players who went on.
- game/stats.rs as_reported (high school stat reporting) is defined but never called.

**Things the reader should label:**
- College record books start empty in 1996, so records_broken shows fills: 802 in 1996, 265 in 1997, then 6-29 a year. The NFL book is seeded with REAL_1983, written from memory.
- All-America picks read the development step's last_performance, not the stats book.
- College EPA uses the NFL expected-points table.

**Real references still from memory or Claude's reading, needing a source:**
- the FBS records in build_data.py
- REAL_1983 in world/pro/honors.rs
- the high school figures in docs/trials/world-trial10.md
- the penalty-kind rates in match_check.rs
- some calendar references

**Not in data/real-world at all:** high school box scores and record books, Heisman and award history, Hall of Fame classes, NFL standings and champions by year, overtime and tie rates, line accuracy, weather splits.

**Other notes:**
- docs/reference/how-it-works/ has no page for the game log, stat book, record books, honors, Hall of Fame or charts. The reader's why text for those has to come from code: records.rs, recruiting.rs honors, college.rs show_pick and the Heisman vote.
- Polls, voters, coaches' hidden ratings, injuries off the field and play-calling internals belong to other parts. I listed them only where game results depend on them.

parts.notes:
Read-only inventory; nothing built or changed. Key facts for the reader's design:
1. The save (crates/afm-engine/src/save.rs: MessagePack with named fields, zstd) holds much more than the export. The export (crates/afm-tools/src/raw.rs write_raw, called from world_trial.rs with AFM_RAW) drops a lot: pros.jsonl keeps only a slice of each season's StatLine (no kicking, punting, returns, blocking, coverage), each contract year only as cap hit and cash, and none of credited, sharpness, ps_seasons, promise, wants_out, rfa, former, expired, spring_snaps, exempt or other-league seasons. nfl_clubs.jsonl is one snapshot at the world's end (payroll, space and dead money for the last year only). nfl_market.jsonl leaves out season_trades, signed_up and trade_funnel. calendar_years.jsonl leaves out the long-road counters and nfl_preseason_games. news.jsonl has no date or refs. Not exported at all: nfl_seasons, nfl_book.careers and candidates, finance, others, stories, storylines, folk, scouting desks and boards, legacy, the seat.
2. History that is not kept anywhere, so a reader cannot show it: past contracts (only the current one), a dated transaction log (signings, cuts, claims, elevations, IR), past GMs and owners, club sales as records, past rosters, schedules, brackets and lines beyond the last two seasons (NflSeason/nfl_prev), combine results per player after the draft, December reads, club boards and public boards after the draft, weather per game, mood, trust, fame and fans over time, gates of past seasons, high school books older than last year, court cases beyond the newest 120 closed ones. The game log's NFL game summaries have only a year: no week, date, line, attendance or weather.
3. The trial-10 world file (/mnt/project-files/afm/worlds/world-2026-seed2026/, 5 parts, 2026-10-20, raw export commit 7594062) predates finance, other leagues, stories, storylines, legacy and parts of scouting. Those fields load empty (serde default). Showing them needs a new world from current main (acfae07).
4. event_history and the game log exist only with keep_game_log, which is trial tooling. In a normal save, past years keep only Big and Huge events (calendar.history), plus the counters in log_history.
5. Some things are computed rather than stored. The reader should call the engine for them: rule books (RuleBook::era, ChangeState::rules), dates (YearDates::new), franchise eras (franchise::name, active_teams), the cap (money::price_cap), weather (weather_in), networks (broadcast.rs), fame and brand (fame.rs), AI head coaches' guidelines (guide.rs), and the people drawn from keys in folk (bosses, boosters, reporters).
6. Real references are uneven. Strong real data: data/real-world/ nfl_rules.json, rookie_scale_2026.csv, combine_by_position.csv, draft_positions_2000_2025.csv, nfl_game_targets.json, engine_targets.json, nfl_schedule_2026.csv, nfl_teams.csv, town_climate.csv and the stories CSVs; also finance/data.rs anchors and the franchise ERAS. Several market targets are "from memory, to verify" (the world_trial.rs nfl_league comment, honors.rs REAL_1983). No real file exists for these, and they are worth adding: careers by round, retirement ages, yearly market counts, trades, arrests, attendance and blackouts by club, award winners by position, early entrants, and agency shares.
7. When showing NFL history game numbers, flag code oddity 14 (docs/reference/how-it-works/oddities.md): history games use today's rule book.
8. Watch the spin-up years. Market and calendar rows start in 1984, before the first recorded year (1996 in trial 10). calendar_years and calendar_events carry a spin_up flag; nfl_market and nfl_trades do not.

areas.name: Known issues layer: code oddities, code against the docs, unconfirmed sizes, open findings
areas.shows: Every place the code is known to do something its own design says it shouldn't (27 oddities as of 2026-10-26), the 'Code against the docs' notes on the system pages, the sizes still marked 'proposed, not confirmed', the trial findings waiting for a yes or no, the parked items, and the systems that run only for your team. With this layer the reader can put a flag on any number a known issue touches, so nobody chases a realism gap that is already a logged bug.
checks: NFL history games all play the 2025 kickoff, the 15-yard extra point and the 10-minute overtime (oddity 14): flag NFL kicking, touchback and scoring numbers for every year before 2025 as 'today's rules' before comparing them to real numbers from that era
College overtime never reaches the two-point shootout (15): count OT games by period reached. Since 2021, real games go to a 3rd OT now and then
Fourth-down choices and EPA use the NFL table at every level (18): flag college and high school EPA and go-rates
A hurt player takes a flat -3 on every rating (5), and injury_check ignores fatigue (6): in-game injury rate by snaps played should show no rise with fatigue. That confirms the oddity is live
AI college and high school teams have no practice injuries (8): compare practice injuries as a share of all injuries, your team against the AI's

missing.notes:
Method: I read every field of pub struct World (crates/afm-engine/src/world/mod.rs), the whole export writer (crates/afm-tools/src/raw.rs write_raw, called from world_trial.rs; tend_by_year.jsonl is written in world_trial.rs itself), the headings of all 16 how-it-works pages, and the struct names across the engine. I then checked the sub-stores most likely missed (stories.media, stories.careers, finance, folk, legacy, scouting, voters, recruiting_log, systems, level_scales).

Almost every World field maps to one of the five readers' areas. What was left is mostly cross-cutting: the known-issues layer (oddities.md and code-against-docs), knobs, a real-reference index with its era holes, the coverage map between world file, game log and export, ids and joins, fitted world numbers, consistency checks, and comparing worlds. The rest are small stores: recruiting_log transfer_seasons and five_stars, pop-culture media, finance.move_up and program history.

Possible overlap: the pop-culture area may partly sit under the NFL reader's 'Media, fame, followers, fans'. Expected wins and luck may partly sit under the programs reader's parity work. I kept them for their specific stored fields.

Main facts for the app builder:
(1) The world file has no game log (World.game_log is serde(skip)). The game's own world files hold no box scores, so game-level realism needs a trial export from the same run.
(2) The export's meta.json has no commit or options, so pairing an export with its world file can't be checked today.
(3) Many newer stores are never exported: finance, folk, stories, storylines, scouting, voters, charts, trends, level_scales, legacy, others, nfl_seasons, deals. The reader should read the world file for those.
(4) Export filters drop high schoolers under 3 stars, keep every 10th high schooler's tendencies, and drop HS-only coaches. player_detail has no body and no id.
(5) hall_of_fame, records_broken, news and calendar_events have no person ids, so their drill-downs break.
(6) 12 spin-up years are recorded with spin_up: true (the sample's calendar_events start in 1984). Checks must leave them out.
(7) Two researched real files are read by no code: data/real-world/coach_effect_*.json and development_injuries.json. They are ready-made real references for coaching effect, age curves, career length and injuries.
(8) Real targets mostly cover NFL 2021-25 and college 2014-25. Early-era and high school real baselines are missing; trial 10's HS numbers were from memory.
